prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Meridian Regional Air Traffic Flow Management and Airport Collaborative Decision-Making System:Regional Flow Platform=Cedarbell;Meridian International Airport/Harbor East Airport/North Valley Airport/Lakeside Regional Airport/Southport Airport retain authority. Aliases:Airline Operations Coordinator=Saffron;Regional Flow Manager=Copperfin;Demand Prediction Service=Marlinstone;Weather Ingest Gateway=Orchard;Airport CDM Portal=Foxglove;Tower Supervisor=Brindle;Ramp Control Lead=Quartzline;Slot Allocation Engine=Blueharbor;Slot Coordinator=Halcyon;Tower Sequence Manager=Ironleaf;Ramp Movement Board=Skylark;Alert Distribution Hub=Lantern. Airline Operations Centre→Airline Interface Adapter→Flight Data Exchange:Flight Intent Message;Identity Access Service authenticates;invalid/incomplete rejected(reason-codes);material intents supersede schedules;changes require messages. Business Rules Registry governs fairness/carriers/spacing/alert-subscriptions. Marlinstone+Capacity Assessment Module→Blueharbor:demand/intents/Airport Capacity Plan/Airport Acceptance Rate/metering/sector-loading. Blueharbor→Adapter/Foxglove:Calculated Takeoff Time/Target Off Block Time/arrival-opportunities;runway/departure-fix/Ground Delay Program constraints;capacity>preferences;safety/emergency/humanitarian/national-obligation>commercial>discretionary;fairness mandatory. Copperfin authorizes Capacity Reduction State exceptions/recovery/divergence;receives departure-rate erosion notifications;chooses near-departure metering/targeted-delay/rerouting/wider-regulation. Halcyon confirms publication,requests delay/fairness adjustments,checks resequencing/Slot Compliance State. Orchard validates weather/provenance/overrides;Storm Cell Snapshot confidence/degradation/provisional-capacity visible;Meteorology Briefing Officer interprets. East Apron Sensor/West Apron Sensor→Skylark→Surface Surveillance Adapter→Foxglove:advisory movements/timestamped milestones. Quartzline reconciles constraints,sends Stand Tow Request Form;Blueharbor recalculates. Brindle/Airport Duty Manager resolve conflicts;Runway Inspection Note precedes capacity endorsement;North Runway Meter/South Runway Meter receive capacities;Lantern distributes approvals. Saffron shall confirm operator-requested revisions before freeze-horizon;justified connection/crew/rotation reviews permitted;stable queues preferred. Ground Handling Dispatcher→Handling Resource Planner:completion

New part:
S345: The Digital Briefing Room provides a common venue for the Regional Flow Manager, Airspace Sector Planner, Military Airspace Liaison, Tower Supervisor, and Airport Duty Manager to confirm the active interpretation of the restriction.
S346: The Performance Analytics Warehouse later compares planned capacity, issued alerts, operator acknowledgements, and realized delay to determine whether the restriction handling process supported timely and consistent decisions.
S347: Departure metering extends the restriction handling process by deciding where delay is best absorbed before aircraft begin taxi.
S348: The Departure Metering Service, known operationally as Emberline, is the system function that converts runway demand into controlled stand delay before aircraft enter the taxi stream.
S349: The metering process starts when the Regional Flow Platform normalizes each Flight Intent Message against the current Airport Capacity Plan.
S350: The Demand Prediction Service estimates the departure demand profile by stand, apron area, runway, and departure fix.
S351: The Capacity Assessment Module compares that demand with the active Airport Acceptance Rate, runway configuration, taxiway constraints, and sector limits.
S352: The Departure Metering Service then derives a feasible Target Off Block Time that protects the Calculated Takeoff Time without overloading the surface movement area.
S353: Stand absorption is preferred when the aircraft can remain connected to normal operator processes and when holding at the gate will not create a gate conflict.
S354: Pushback windows are coordinated as narrow time bands that give the flight crew, ramp team, and tower sequence a common expectation without treating the window as a clearance to move.
S355: Blueharbor shall adjust allocated departure times when metering rules require additional stand absorption to preserve the planned runway sequence.
S356: Halcyon records the agreed pushback window rationale in the coordination notes before the plan is released to operational users.
S357: The Ramp Control Lead reviews the proposed windows against apron congestion, towing activity, and aircraft readiness before accepting them for local execution.
S358: The Tower Supervisor monitors whether the planned release rate remains compatible with departure spacing and runway crossing demand.
S359: The North Runway Meter and South Runway Meter maintain independent queue counts so that one runway cannot mask an excess queue on the other runway.
S360: Surface surveillance inputs from the Surface Surveillance Adapter are used to confirm the actual number of aircraft waiting at runway holding points.
S361: The Ramp Movement Board produces the Fuel Truck Hold Advice when metering decisions require servicing activity to remain clear of an aircraft that is being held at stand.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
